calibration.reason: The repair intake is legible and clearly labeled, but its familiar layout limits distinctiveness and misplaced focus after invalid input impairs recovery.

primary_action.input: Tab to the 6 m footbridge row and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show the path and footbridge closed and ferry stopped.
primary_action.observed: The value changed to 6 m and all three statuses updated as expected. The focused row had a visible outline.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter set 2 m. The path was closed; ferry and footbridge were marked level not reached.
A-1440.fact_check: The captured 6 m water line appears between the 4 m and 6 m marks, inconsistent with the 6 m text. The stated closure thresholds are internally consistent, but their real-world accuracy is unsupported.
A-1440.strength: The cross-section, scale and closure rows form a clear editorial composition.
A-1440.weakness: The water graphic conflicts with the selected value, undermining the central comparison.
A-1440.repair: Synchronize the water surface with the labeled scale and verify it at each threshold.

primary_action.input: Tab four times to the 6 m row and press Enter.
primary_action.expected: Set 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The value and all three statuses updated. The complete result was readable within the 390 × 844 initial viewport.

A-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab twice and Enter set 2 m; only the path was marked closed, while the other two levels were not reached.
A-390.fact_check: At the captured 6 m state, the water surface appears above 4 m but below 6 m. Actual local closure thresholds are not independently verified.
A-390.strength: The full cross-section, control and status list fit together in the first viewport.
A-390.weakness: The small diagram makes labels compact, and its water line contradicts the displayed value.
A-390.repair: Correct the water-to-scale mapping and retain legible labels at mobile size.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected radio and press ArrowRight twice.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: The 6 m radio became selected, the list showed path closes, ferry stops and footbridge closes, and the water reached the 6 m line.

B-1440.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses returned to 2 m and the list contained only Riverside path closes.
B-1440.fact_check: The captured water height aligns with the selected 6 m marker and all three diagram labels are highlighted. Actual local closure thresholds are not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: The selected level, concise result and illustrated cross-section reinforce one another.
B-1440.weakness: The diagram's decorative terrain and large heading occupy substantial space relative to the task.
B-1440.repair: Reduce the header or illustration footprint while preserving the clear result and scale.

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected radio and press ArrowRight twice.
primary_action.expected: Select 6 m and show all three closures.
primary_action.observed: All three list items appeared, the 6 m radio showed focus, and the water aligned with the 6 m marker. The complete result and diagram were readable within the 390 × 844 initial viewport.

B-390.edge_observation: Two ArrowLeft presses returned to 2 m; the list contained only Riverside path closes.
B-390.fact_check: The 6 m visual and text agree in the captured state. Actual local closure thresholds are not independently verified.
B-390.strength: The controls and complete closure list precede the diagram and remain visible without scrolling.
B-390.weakness: The diagram labels crowd the small illustration, especially around the crossing drawings.
B-390.repair: Give the mobile diagram labels more separation from the illustrated features.

preference.reason: Both views support the requested keyboard actions and fit the complete mobile result in the tested viewport. B's 6 m water surface aligns with its scale and text, while A's captured surface remains below 6 m.

decision: The candidate still beats the stock control. The round 6 layout lost ground against round 5 because the terrain competes with the answer and crowds mobile labels. Retain round 5. Round 7 separates the labels and simplifies the crossing figures.
